title: AI First book content
description: Structure of a books/*.json file. Global id uniqueness is enforced separately by scripts/validate.ts, since JSON Schema cannot check uniqueness across files.

tag.description: Short id prefix for this book's exercises, e.g. "py" in py-2-06. Declared, not inferred, so adding a book needs no code change.

language.description: Language id, matching VS Code's (python, java, ...).

response.description: Canonical response. An array is joined with newlines; both forms must round-trip byte-identically to the printed book.

title.description: Must lead with 'Chapter N:' — the chapter number is parsed from it.

examples.description: May be empty: chapters are authored ahead of their examples.

example.description: Authored either as a single prompt/response pair or as a `prompts` array of progressive steps — never both.

expectsException.description: The exercise ends by throwing an uncaught exception on purpose, to demonstrate an error, so exiting non-zero is the correct outcome. Stored because CI must reach the same verdict as the authoring run without a model.

stdin.description: Sample input for an exercise that reads stdin. Required whenever the response reads input (enforced by scripts/validate.ts): an assistant cannot type into a running program, so without a sample these exercises could never be completed through one.

kind.description: How runnable the example is. `program` runs as a single file; `class` has no entry point; `test` needs a test runner; `project` needs several files. Defaults to program.

status.description: Publication state; omit when published. `draft` is imported from a manuscript but not yet explained or proved to run. `retired` is no longer in the book, kept only so an existing learner progress entry still refers to something. Neither is served to readers.

explanation.description: Pre-computed walkthrough of the response. Stored rather than generated at runtime so a reader sees the same words in the CLI and in the VS Code extension, which has no model.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what the code does.

lines.description: Line-by-line notes. Only the lines worth commenting on, in source order.

code.description: The line of code, verbatim from the response.

run.description: Human-readable note on how to run it.

scaffold.description: Extra files that make a non-runnable example runnable. The response itself is never modified -- it stays byte-exact to the printed page -- so anything needed around it lives here.

fromExercise.description: Reuse another exercise's response as this file's content, so the two cannot drift apart. Mutually exclusive with content.

entrypoint.description: Which file to execute, when it is not the exercise's own file.
